body:
[SIPHONED VERDICT]: The Bushehr strikes present an attribution gap with a nuclear-adjacent facility at its center. Iran says US-Israeli projectiles struck the nuclear plant perimeter. The US says it didn't. Both parties then went silent. Physical evidence — FirMS thermal data, SAR imagery, commercial satellite imagery — would resolve whether the strikes happened at the coordinates Iran named. Until then, the attribution gap is the story.

On Thursday July 9, Iranian state media reported multiple explosions across southern Iran — in Bushehr province (including near the perimeter of Iran's Russian-built nuclear power plant), Konarak, Choghadak, and Bandar Abbas. Ehsan Jahanian, the political and security deputy governor of Bushehr province, told state media that a military facility near Bushehr city was struck by what he described as "US-Israeli enemy projectiles." A local official told Iranian state media a US projectile had struck the perimeter of the nuclear facility — an area previously hit during the April–July conflict.

The US response was immediate denial. A US official told Reuters flatly: "The US military was not conducting strikes in Iran at the time of the reported attacks." CENTCOM said nothing. Secretary of State and Defense officials have not claimed the strikes. No US official has acknowledged any strike near Bushehr on July 9–10.

Hours later, Iranian state media reported new strikes on Konarak (hit twice) and another military site in Bushehr — again attributing to "enemy forces." The Americans again said nothing. Since then: complete silence from all parties on attribution.

IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi said his agency was monitoring the situation at Bushehr, would not confirm damage, and stated that attacking any nuclear plant would be "unacceptable." Iranian officials have blamed "enemy forces" throughout; US officials have denied.

The attribution gap is the OSINT story. Multiple scenarios fit the physical evidence:
1. Israeli unilateral strikes (Netanyahu has explicitly warned of resuming Iran campaign "with even greater force")
2. US-Israeli coordinated strikes denied by Washington
3. False-flag Iranian operations to justify escalation
4. Internal IRGC faction action
5. Unknown third-party actor

Physical evidence available: FIRMS thermal satellite data would show heat signatures at the reported strike sites — Bushehr military site, Konarak, Choghadak — on July 9. Sentinel-1 SAR imagery from ESA would show structural damage at the nuclear plant perimeter. Commercial imagery (Planet Labs, Maxar) of the Bushehr nuclear plant perimeter would confirm whether the reported "US projectile hit perimeter" left craters or structural damage. The IAEA visit/access status to Bushehr is a verifiable fact — has inspectors been allowed in since July 9?

Context: this escalation comes as Iran was burying Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei (killed February 28). Iran's new leadership is in transition. Three of Khamenei's sons attended the funeral; Mojtaba Khamenei — widely viewed as the military's preferred successor — did not attend, reportedly still in hiding. The strikes occurred during maximum institutional vulnerability.

The asymmetry (Iran blames, US denies, both go silent) is itself the finding. Compare to prior incidents where US eventually confirmed strikes days after denial. The FirMS thermal data and SAR imagery from July 9–10 would show whether the strikes happened at the coordinates Iran named. The absence of that evidence, combined with the absence of any US acknowledgment, leaves the attribution question open and the nuclear facility's damage status unconfirmed.
narrative: The story is not 'who struck Bushehr' — it's that there is NO authoritative attribution chain while a nuclear-adjacent facility was struck, the IAEA cannot confirm damage, and a ceasefire is technically still supposed to be in force. The asymmetry (Iran blames, US denies, both go silent) is structurally similar to prior incidents where attribution remained disputed for days before physical evidence surfaced.
analysis: Iran has repeatedly blamed 'US-Israeli enemy projectiles' for incidents throughout the war and been partially or fully correct some of the time. The current pattern — Iranian official attribution plus US denial plus then silence from both — fits a specific structure: one party names coordinates and weapon type; the other party denies; neither provides evidence. The FirMS and SAR imagery available within days of the strikes will show whether the thermal signatures and structural damage match Iran's account. Until then, the attribution gap with a nuclear-adjacent facility at its center is the only definitive fact on record.
